transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Lina Torres, Jamal Reed (Redwood) — Dr. Maya Chen, Alex Rivera, Priya Singh (Sequoia Medical)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to onboard Sequoia Medical onto Redwood Dedicated capacity. Discussed security, networking (VPC), pilot scope and initial benchmarks.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE on the account, with Lina our SE and Jamal the CSM. Maya, Alex, Priya, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Dr. Maya Chen: Thanks, Samir. Quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, CTO, Alex handles data infra, Priya is security. We're excited but we have a few must-haves around PHI handling and residency.
[00:33] Samir: Totally, that's why we suggested dedicated initially — gives you capacity isolation, and we can enable VPC + customer-managed KMS. Lina will go through the technical bits.
[00:45] Lina: Hi folks. Quick note, sorry if audio drops, there's a tiny echo. So architecture overview: for Dedicated we provision GPU pools, we support private VPC peering or private link, and you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. We also expose audit logs and trace per request.
[01:05] Alex Rivera: When you say audit logs, what retention and format? We need logs for three years for some workflows.
[01:15] Lina: Right now we have configurable retention; default is 90 days in the console but enterprise add-on can extend — logs are JSON with request metadata + model/version + route. We'll share the schema. (mumble) sometimes the log names in console show redwd-infer instead of redwood-infer in early builds, sorry that's a small transcription thing.
[01:39] Priya Singh: On encryption — is customer-managed key required for PHI? We want to ensure keys never leave our KMS.
[01:48] Samir: It's optional but recommended. With Private and Dedicated we support bring-your-own-KMS and HSM integration; keys stay in your KMS, Redwood only gets wrapped tokens. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[02:05] Dr. Maya Chen: Good. Also, about data residency — we need processing to happen in us-west-2 region only.
[02:13] Lina: We can pin the region for Dedicated nodes, yes. For Hosted it's multi-region and harder to guarantee. We'll note region pinning as part of the config.
[02:26] Alex: Great. Now on workload — our initial pilot will be triage scoring and summarization of visit notes, roughly 10k requests/day with avg 300 tokens in/out.
[02:36] Lina: For that profile, we recommend a 1-2 GPU pool to start with ability to autoscale bursts; we can show estimated tokens-per-dollar in the benchmark. Also consider KV cache for repeated prefixes — that'll lower token spend.
[02:50] Samir: Quick tradeoff here — you can run hosted to start faster but for PHI/dedicated SLA you probably want Dedicated. Cost delta depends on utilization; Lina will provide estimates.
[03:05] Dr. Maya Chen: Timeline question — we need pilot live by end of Q1. Is that realistic?
[03:12] Jamal: Yes, that's achievable. We'll do onboarding + environment access in week 1, benchmark and tuning week 2, then pilot run week 3-8.
[03:20] Priya: Security review — we need SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary, SSO/SAML integration, and audit of RBAC.
[03:28] Samir: We'll attach SOC2 and recent pentest summary. SSO via SAML/Okta supported. RBAC configurable in console, and we can map groups via SCIM.
[03:40] Alex: For perf testing, do you provide sample harness or do we need to run our own?
[03:45] Lina: We have a perf harness and scripts; we'll run a short run using your sample dataset if you provide anonymized samples or synthetic equivalents. We'll also share the benchmarking spreadsheet.
[03:58] Dr. Maya Chen: About model choice — we want an open model if possible; cost is a concern but quality cannot degrade. Any recommendations?
[04:07] Lina: We have validated variants; for clinical text summarization some teams prefer a finetuned open model run on 8-bit quantization for cost; for higher quality you can choose a non-quantized variant. We'll include model recommendations in the doc.
[04:22] (crosstalk) Alex: Do you support automatic fallback to cheaper model when load spikes?
[04:27] Lina: Yes, smart routing policies allow fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency vs cost). That's configurable per route.
[04:35] Priya: Logging question again — will logs include PHI? We can't have raw PHI retained in logs.
[04:42] Jamal: By default request metadata logs request IDs and token counts; payload redaction is an option — we can disable storing full prompts and responses in logs for compliance. We'll make sure that's in the onboarding checklist.
[04:57] Samir: Quick note on SLA — Dedicated comes with 99.9% uptime and latency targets; we'll include SLOs in the contract but let's get the pilot running first.
[05:08] Dr. Maya Chen: Ok. Procurement — who will own contracts on your side?
[05:15] Samir: Our Legal (cc'd in follow-ups) will own contracts; I can loop them in. For payment we support PO or card for initial months.
[05:24] Alex: Any prerequisites we need to prep?
[05:28] Lina: Provide a VPC CIDR block for peering, sample payloads (anonymized), and list of IPs for allowlist. Priya should send compliance docs list.
[05:38] Priya: Will do. Also, can we get demo of Console for routing and rollouts?
[05:44] Jamal: Yes, CSM will run a Console walkthrough as part of training.
[05:49] Samir: Ok let's recap next steps. Lina will run the benchmark, Samir will send docs and pricing, Jamal will schedule training. Do we want the SE deep dive the week of Jan 10?
[05:59] Dr. Maya Chen: That works for us.
[06:02] Alex: One more question — how is KV cache managed? Is it per-customer or global?
[06:09] Lina: Per-customer and per-route. It's sticky to the model variant and sequence pref. It helps with repeated patient note prefixes. We'll detail how TTL and invalidation works in the doc.
[06:22] [long silence, typing noises]
[25:00] (transcription jumps forward due to upload) Lina: ...and this is the benchmark spreadsheet link we uploaded: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/sequoia-sample (note: link transcribed imperfectly).
[25:18] Dr. Maya Chen: I see the tail latencies — can we get 95th percentile under 250ms for the summarization route?
[25:25] Lina: Depends on batch config and GPU type; for A100-class hardware it's achievable with tuning and smaller batch windows. We'll try to target that in the run.
[25:40] Priya: Anything else on compliance?
[25:44] Samir: We'll include SOC2 and pen test summary in the email. Also, we'll provide the SAAS addendum and DPA.
[25:54] Alex: Great, please include pricing scenarios: sustained vs bursty.
[26:00] Samir: Yes, pricing sheet will show dedicated commit vs on-demand math.
[26:10] Jamal: I'll schedule the Console walkthrough and training session, and add notes to the onboarding project in our tracker.
[26:20] Dr. Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.
[26:25] Samir: Thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and dates.
[26:30] (call ends)
